sentences.hint: Bild: ein hilfsbereites, aber ungeschicktes Tier aus einer Fabel
sentences.english: With his excessive defence the spokesman did his party leader a disservice.

sentences.sentence: Erst die Recherche einer Lokalzeitung brachte den ____ ins Rollen. (set things in motion)
sentences.english: It was only a local newspaper’s investigation that set things in motion.

help.intro: Educated German (Bildungssprache) draws on a stock of Latin-derived words and phrases that rarely occur in everyday talk but run through every quality newspaper, court judgment and academic text: evident, eruieren, obsolet, prekär, konzedieren, implizieren, subsumieren, stringent, sukzessive, and set Latin phrases such as a priori, de facto, per se, ad hoc, Status quo and sui generis. At C2 you must read them without hesitation and use them precisely in your own essays. In this quiz the German line above each sentence gives a plain paraphrase and the cue gives the English; type the Fremdwort, inflected to fit the sentence (prekären, konzediert, eruiert). Adjectives and verbs follow normal German grammar; the Latin phrases never inflect. Watch out for false friends with English: eventuell means possibly, not eventually, and konsequent means consistent, not consequent.

tips.title: German grammar on Latin stems
tips.text: Verbs in -ieren are regular and take no ge- in the Partizip II: eruieren → eruiert, konzedieren → konzediert, implizieren → impliziert, subsumieren → subsumiert. Adjectives take normal endings: unter prekären Bedingungen, eine stringente Argumentation, ein obsoletes Verfahren. Nouns keep their gender: das Desiderat, die Prämisse, der Status quo, das Diktum.

examples.de: Die Ursache des Ausfalls konnte bislang nicht eruiert werden.
examples.en: The cause of the outage has not yet been ascertained.

examples.de: Die Autorin konzediert, dass ihre Stichprobe klein ist.
examples.en: The author concedes that her sample is small.

tips.trap: geeruiert or gekonzediert do not exist: verbs in -ieren never take ge-.

tips.title: Latin phrases stay invariable
tips.text: a priori (von vornherein), a posteriori (aus der Erfahrung, im Nachhinein), de facto (tatsächlich) vs de jure (rechtlich), per se (an sich), ad hoc (eigens, spontan), sui generis (eigener Art), Status quo (bestehender Zustand), ceteris paribus (unter sonst gleichen Bedingungen). They take no endings; only Status quo behaves like a noun with an article: den Status quo wahren.

examples.de: De jure ist der Präsident Oberbefehlshaber, de facto entscheidet das Parlament.
examples.en: In law the president is commander-in-chief; in practice parliament decides.

examples.de: Ob sich die Maßnahme bewährt, lässt sich erst a posteriori beurteilen.
examples.en: Whether the measure proves itself can only be judged in retrospect.

tips.title: Precision, not decoration
tips.text: Each Fremdwort says something the everyday word does not quite say. evident is stronger than klar; stringent describes the logic of an argument, not its strictness; marginal means negligible in extent; ambivalent means torn between two feelings, not indifferent; kontraproduktiv means working against one’s own goal. Use one where it sharpens the statement — a sentence stuffed with Latinisms reads as pompous.

examples.de: Die Unterschiede sind marginal und ändern nichts am Ergebnis.
examples.en: The differences are negligible and change nothing about the result.

examples.de: Ein Boykott wäre in dieser Phase kontraproduktiv.
examples.en: A boycott would be counter-productive at this stage.

tips.trap: ambivalent is not indifferent (gleichgültig): an ambivalent person feels two things at once.

tips.title: Beware of English look-alikes
tips.text: Several Latinate words mean something different in German. eventuell = possibly (eventually = schließlich); konsequent = consistent, rigorous (consequent = folgend); sensibel = sensitive (sensible = vernünftig); prägnant = concise (pregnant = schwanger); rentabel = profitable. Check every look-alike before you use it in an essay.

examples.de: Die Regierung hat die Reform konsequent umgesetzt.
examples.en: The government implemented the reform consistently.

examples.de: Wir kommen eventuell etwas später.
examples.en: We may possibly come a bit later.

table.caption: Latinisms and their plain German equivalents

remember: Verbs in -ieren: no ge- in the Partizip II (eruiert, konzediert, impliziert).
Adjectives inflect normally (unter prekären Bedingungen); Latin phrases never do (a priori, de facto, per se, ad hoc).
Use a Fremdwort for precision, not decoration — one per sentence is usually enough.
False friends: eventuell = possibly, konsequent = consistent, sensibel = sensitive.

context.de: Dass die bisherige Förderpraxis obsolet ist, gilt in der Fachwelt als evident. Umstritten ist hingegen, wie sie zu ersetzen wäre. Die Kommission soll zunächst eruieren, welche Betriebe de facto profitieren; erst dann lässt sich die Prämisse prüfen, dass Subventionen per se Innovation fördern. Selbst die Befürworter konzedieren, dass eine stringente Evaluation bislang ein Desiderat geblieben ist. Die Umstellung soll daher sukzessive erfolgen und nicht ad hoc.
context.en: That the previous funding practice is obsolete is regarded among experts as self-evident. What is disputed, by contrast, is how it should be replaced. The commission is first to ascertain which businesses actually benefit; only then can the premise that subsidies promote innovation in themselves be tested. Even the supporters concede that a rigorous evaluation has so far remained a desideratum. The changeover is therefore to take place gradually and not at short notice.

mistakes.wrong: Die Zahl der Betroffenen wurde geeruiert.
mistakes.right: Die Zahl der Betroffenen wurde eruiert.
mistakes.why: Verbs in -ieren form the Partizip II without ge-.

mistakes.wrong: Nach langem Streit einigten sie sich eventuell.
mistakes.right: Nach langem Streit einigten sie sich schließlich.
mistakes.why: eventuell means possibly; for eventually German uses schließlich or letztendlich.
A Latin-derived adjective before a noun takes the normal German ending.

mistakes.wrong: Die Bevölkerung ist dem Projekt gegenüber ambivalent, es ist ihr egal.
mistakes.right: Die Bevölkerung ist dem Projekt gegenüber gleichgültig.
mistakes.why: ambivalent means torn between opposing feelings, not indifferent.

help.exam: At C2 the reading paper’s academic and journalistic texts use Latinate vocabulary freely, and gap-fill and matching tasks test whether you can tell evident from eventuell or de facto from de jure. In the writing task, a few precise Fremdwörter raise the register of an essay — as long as they are used correctly and not piled up.

sentences.english: Even the reform’s harshest critic concedes that it has noticeably relieved the administration.

sentences.english: The wording in the minutes implies that the board knew about the losses.

sentences.english: Very different activities can be subsumed under the term “care work”.

sentences.english: The author’s argument is rigorous and free of contradictions.

sentences.english: The transition periods are to expire gradually so that businesses can adapt.

sentences.english: One cannot rule out from the outset that the measure will have undesirable side effects.

sentences.hint: lateinische Wendung, Gegenbegriff zu de jure
sentences.english: Officially the ban still applies, but in practice it has not been enforced for years.

sentences.sentence: Wachstum ist nicht ____ gut; entscheidend ist, wem es zugutekommt. (in itself)
sentences.english: Growth is not good in itself; what matters is who benefits from it.

sentences.english: The working group was convened at short notice after the first damage had become known.

sentences.english: Anyone who blocks every reform entrenches the status quo.

sentences.english: A long-term study of the consequences remains an urgent desideratum of research.

sentences.english: The entire calculation rests on the premise that interest rates stay low.

quizzes.title: C2.2 · Deutsch in Österreich und der Schweiz

help.intro: German is a pluricentric language: Germany, Austria and Switzerland each have their own standard variety, and Austrian and Swiss Standard German are no less correct than the German spoken in Hamburg — they are not dialects. They differ above all in vocabulary: Austria says Jänner, Paradeiser, Erdäpfel, Marillen, Topfen, Obers, Matura, Trafik and heuer; Switzerland says Velo, parkieren, grillieren, Trottoir, Billett, Znüni, Estrich (attic) and allenfalls (if necessary); both say Spital. There are also a few grammar differences, such as the perfect with sein (ich bin gesessen), and Swiss spelling never uses ß. At C2 you read Austrian and Swiss newspapers, official letters and recipes without stumbling. In this quiz the German line tells you the region and the word used in Germany; type the Austrian or Swiss standard word — or, in the two items marked with an arrow, the German-German equivalent.

tips.title: Austria: the kitchen and the calendar
tips.text: Jänner (Januar), Paradeiser (Tomaten), Erdäpfel (Kartoffeln), Marillen (Aprikosen), Topfen (Quark), Obers / Schlagobers (Sahne), Karfiol (Blumenkohl), Kren (Meerrettich), Sessel (Stuhl), Matura (Abitur), Trafik (Tabak- und Zeitschriftenladen), heuer (dieses Jahr). When Austria joined the EU in 1995, a protocol gave 23 Austrian food terms — among them Erdäpfel, Marillen, Topfen, Paradeiser and Obers — equal legal standing with their German-German counterparts.

examples.de: Heuer gibt es besonders viele Marillen.
examples.en: This year there are particularly many apricots.

examples.de: Die Matura findet im Mai statt.
examples.en: The school-leaving exam takes place in May.

tips.trap: Sessel in Austria is an ordinary chair; the upholstered armchair is a Fauteuil.

tips.title: Switzerland: French loans and -ieren
tips.text: Swiss Standard German borrows from French and likes the ending -ieren: Velo (Fahrrad), Trottoir (Gehweg), Billett (Fahrkarte), Poulet (Hähnchen), Glace (Eis), parkieren (parken), grillieren (grillen). Everyday life has its own words: Znüni (mid-morning snack), Estrich (Dachboden), Gesuch (Antrag), Busse (Geldstrafe), allenfalls (gegebenenfalls), Matur or Matura (Abitur). Spital (Krankenhaus) is standard in both Switzerland and Austria.

examples.de: Das Velo darf nicht auf dem Trottoir parkiert werden.
examples.en: The bike may not be parked on the pavement.

examples.de: Allfällige Fragen beantworten wir gern; allenfalls rufen wir Sie zurück.
examples.en: We are happy to answer any questions; if necessary we will call you back.

tips.trap: Estrich in Germany is floor screed; in Switzerland it is the attic. allenfalls in Germany means at most, in Switzerland if necessary.

tips.title: Grammar and spelling
tips.text: In Austria, Switzerland and southern Germany sitzen, stehen and liegen form the perfect with sein: Ich bin gesessen, Das Auto ist vor dem Haus gestanden, Er ist im Bett gelegen. Swiss Standard German writes ss wherever Germany and Austria write ß: Strasse, Grüsse, schliesslich, gross. Some genders differ too: in Austria das Cola and das E-Mail are common, and in Switzerland das Tram.

examples.de: Wir sind lange vor dem Eingang gestanden.
examples.en: We stood in front of the entrance for a long time.

examples.de: Mit freundlichen Grüssen aus der Gemeindeverwaltung
examples.en: With kind regards from the municipal administration

tips.title: Standard, not dialect
tips.text: Everything in this quiz is written standard language: it appears in newspapers, laws, school books and official letters in Austria or Switzerland. Dialect is something else — Swiss German dialects (Schweizerdeutsch) and Austrian dialects are spoken varieties you are not expected to write. So Velo and Jänner belong in a C2 text; dialect spellings do not.

examples.de: Der Nationalrat tritt im Jänner wieder zusammen.
examples.en: The National Council reconvenes in January.

examples.de: Das Billett gilt nur für die zweite Klasse.
examples.en: The ticket is only valid for second class.

table.caption: Standard words in Germany, Austria and Switzerland

remember: Austrian and Swiss Standard German are standard varieties, not dialects.
Austria: Jänner, Paradeiser, Erdäpfel, Marillen, Topfen, Obers, Matura, Trafik, heuer.
Switzerland: Velo, Trottoir, Billett, Znüni, Estrich, parkieren, grillieren, allenfalls; no ß.
South of the Main: ich bin gesessen / gestanden / gelegen.

context.de: Heuer ist die Wienerin Anna nach der Matura für ein Praktikum nach Zürich gezogen. Anfangs ist sie oft ratlos vor dem Fahrplan gestanden: Statt einer Fahrkarte löst man dort ein Billett, zur Arbeit fährt man mit dem Velo, und wer falsch parkiert, zahlt eine Busse. Im Büro gibt es um zehn das Znüni, und ihre Wohnung hat einen Estrich, wo sie die Koffer verstaut. Nur beim Einkaufen vermisst sie ihre Marillen und den Topfen — in Zürich heißen sie Aprikosen und Quark.
context.en: This year, after her school-leaving exam, Anna from Vienna moved to Zurich for an internship. At first she often stood baffled in front of the timetable: instead of a Fahrkarte you buy a Billett there, you ride your Velo to work, and anyone who parks wrongly pays a fine. At the office there is the Znüni at ten, and her flat has an attic where she stores her suitcases. Only when shopping does she miss her Marillen and her Topfen — in Zurich they are called apricots and quark.

mistakes.wrong: Schweizerdeutsch und Schweizer Hochdeutsch sind dasselbe.
mistakes.right: Schweizerdeutsch ist Dialekt; Schweizer Hochdeutsch ist die geschriebene Standardsprache.
mistakes.why: Words like Velo and Billett belong to the written standard, not to dialect.

mistakes.wrong: Wir haben die Koffer in den Estrich gebracht. (in Germany, meaning the attic)
mistakes.right: Wir haben die Koffer auf den Dachboden gebracht.
mistakes.why: In Germany Estrich is floor screed; only in Switzerland is it the attic.

mistakes.wrong: Ich habe gesessen ist in Österreich falsch.
mistakes.right: In Österreich ist ich bin gesessen üblich; ich habe gesessen wird aber verstanden.
mistakes.why: The perfect with sein for sitzen/stehen/liegen is a regional standard feature, not an error either way.

help.exam: At C2 the reading and listening papers may use authentic texts from Austria or Switzerland — a Viennese newspaper report, a Swiss official notice, a recipe — and expect you to understand regional standard words such as Jänner, Spital or Velo without comment. In your own writing, stay consistent within one variety.

sentences.english: According to the Vienna municipal authority’s decision, the deadline ends on 31 January 2027.

sentences.sentence: Die Wachau ist berühmt für ihre ____, aus denen Knödel, Marmelade und Brände gemacht werden. (apricots)
sentences.english: The Wachau is famous for its apricots, which are made into dumplings, jam and brandies.

sentences.sentence: Für den Strudel braucht man 500 Gramm ____, zwei Eier und etwas Zitronenschale. (curd cheese)
sentences.english: For the strudel you need 500 grams of curd cheese, two eggs and some lemon zest.

sentences.sentence: Nach der ____ will sie in Graz Medizin studieren. (school-leaving exam)
sentences.english: After her school-leaving exam she wants to study medicine in Graz.

sentences.sentence: ____ findet das Festival zum ersten Mal schon im Juni statt. (this year)
sentences.english: This year the festival is taking place in June for the first time.

sentences.sentence: Den Kaffee nehme ich mit einem Schuss ____, bitte. (cream)
sentences.hint: Milchprodukt; geschlagen kommt es auf den Strudel
sentences.english: I’ll have my coffee with a dash of cream, please.

sentences.sentence: Die Zeitung und einen Fahrschein bekommen Sie in der ____ an der Ecke. (tobacconist’s kiosk)
sentences.english: You can get the newspaper and a ticket at the tobacconist’s on the corner.

sentences.sentence: Wenn ein Wiener im Möbelhaus einen „Sessel“ verlangt, meint er, was man in Hamburg einen ____ nennt. (chair)
sentences.english: When a Viennese asks for a “Sessel” in a furniture shop, he means what is called a chair in Hamburg.

sentences.sentence: Wir ____ zwei Stunden im Kaffeehaus gesessen und haben Zeitung gelesen. (have sat)
sentences.english: We sat in the coffee house for two hours reading the paper.

sentences.sentence: Der Verletzte wurde mit der Ambulanz ins ____ gebracht. (hospital)
sentences.english: The injured man was taken to hospital by ambulance.

sentences.sentence: Wer in Basel zur Arbeit pendelt, nimmt bei jedem Wetter das ____. (bicycle)
sentences.english: Anyone commuting to work in Basel takes the bike in all weathers.

sentences.sentence: Wer im Halteverbot ____, riskiert eine Busse. (parks)
sentences.english: Anyone who parks in a no-stopping zone risks a fine.

sentences.sentence: Die Kinder sollen auf dem ____ warten, bis die Ampel grün ist. (pavement)
sentences.english: The children are to wait on the pavement until the lights turn green.

sentences.sentence: Um zehn Uhr gibt es in der Firma das ____: Kaffee, Gipfeli und etwas Obst. (mid-morning snack)
sentences.english: At ten o’clock the company has its mid-morning break: coffee, croissants and some fruit.

sentences.sentence: Das ____ für die Fahrt nach Bern können Sie am Automaten oder in der App lösen. (ticket)
sentences.english: You can buy the ticket for the journey to Bern at the machine or in the app.

sentences.sentence: In einer Zürcher Wohnungsanzeige bezeichnet „Estrich“ nicht den Unterboden, sondern den ____. (attic)
sentences.english: In a Zurich flat advert, “Estrich” does not mean the subfloor but the attic.

sentences.sentence: Am Nationalfeiertag wird in vielen Gärten und an den Seeufern ____. (barbecued)
sentences.english: On the national holiday people barbecue in many gardens and on the lakeshores.

sentences.sentence: Wir prüfen Ihr Gesuch und melden uns ____ noch einmal bei Ihnen. (if necessary)
sentences.english: We will examine your application and get back to you if necessary.

sentences.sentence: Der Brief an die Gemeinde endet in Schweizer Rechtschreibung mit „Freundliche ____“. (regards, Swiss spelling)
sentences.english: In Swiss spelling, the letter to the municipality ends with “Freundliche Grüsse”.

help.intro: Every word the C2.2 exercises use, on one deck of flashcards: 303 cards, 123 of them nouns. The vocabulary of this module is precise, stylistically marked vocabulary: register pairs, legal and philosophical terms, and fixed expressions, from the themes Philosophie & Gesellschaft, Wissenschaftssprache, Recht & Verwaltung: Amtsdeutsch, Literatur: Lyrik & Deutung. Write the German, choose it from four options, or flip the card and rate yourself. A word you miss comes back later in the same run, and stays in your weak words until you get it right three times in a row.

tips.title: Register is part of the meaning
tips.text: At C2 two words can mean the same and still not be interchangeable. The note on the back often names the plain or colloquial equivalent; learn which one fits a formal text.

tips.title: Three modes, three kinds of memory
tips.text: Choose trains recognition, Write trains recall, and Flip trains honesty with yourself. Start a new deck in Choose, move to Write once most cards feel familiar, and use Flip for a fast review before an exam.

tips.title: A noun without its article is marked wrong
tips.text: In Write mode a noun only counts with der, die or das in front of it. The card tells you when you had the right word but left the article off, so you know exactly what to fix.

remember: Never say a noun without its article, not even in your head.
Miss a word? It comes back in the same run. Three correct answers in a row take it off the weak list.
Verbs and adjectives have no article: type them as they stand, like "selbst".
help.exam: C2 exam: the texts are authentic journalism, essays and official letters, and the written tasks are marked on precise, register-appropriate word choice.
